hook.line: A crew member fixing his mic asks 'Everything all right, man?' and he says he'll feel better after he says this.
hook.visual: Tight shot of a man in a beige polo backstage while hands clip on his mic, then a wide of a crew member checking on him; short white captions.

beats.what: Backstage mic fitting; nervous small talk sets up a confession-style announcement.
Cut to a sit-down confessional shot; a lower third names him as the brand's CEO.
Dramatic pause on 'as of today, officially...' as if announcing a breakup or shutdown.
Reveal: a product dashboard with a brand visibility gauge cuts in on 'HubSpot AEO'.
Back to him teasing the audience for thinking the brand was done.
Dashboard gauge rises from a low score to 16% on 'it was a mess... then HubSpot'.
Screen recording of a 'Recommended Actions' list (blog posts, social, outreach).
Recommendation detail with tracked AI prompts and citing domains, a cursor pointing at it.
Off-camera director asks for another take; he swears, kicks the stool and storms out.
End card on deep red: product logo with 'Less Drama. More Leads.' and 'Try'.

characters.who: The brand founder playing a dramatic version of himself
characters.enters: Already on screen being mic'd backstage, then seated for the confessional.
characters.acts: Delivers a fake-serious announcement, teases the audience, then has a mock meltdown at the director's note.
characters.exits: Swears, knocks over the stool and walks out of frame.

characters.enters: Crew member's hands and face in the opening backstage shots; director only as a voice later.
characters.acts: Checks on him at the start; later asks for another take, which triggers the meltdown.
characters.exits: Crew leaves after the first shots; director stays off camera.

why_it_works: Fake-breakup announcement framing ('as of today, officially...') makes the viewer expect bad news, so the product reveal lands as a twist.
Product UI appears only as proof inside the story (a gauge going up, a to-do list), not as a separate pitch.
Meltdown blooper after the pitch is a second payoff that rewards watching to the end and fits the 'zero crash outs' joke.
Cuts every 3.4 s (median) keep a 72 s ad moving.
weaknesses: 37% of the runtime is silence; long dramatic pauses could lose scrollers before the reveal at 22 s.
73% of the on-screen text sits outside the safe area, so TikTok's UI can cover captions.
The product's name is not said until 22 s, so viewers who leave earlier never learn what it was for.
for_robert: Use the 'serious announcement, then twist' setup: Robert announces gravely, cut to the proof on screen, and end with an out-of-character blooper where Fred breaks the take and storms out of frame.
